cards.front: Dropped from height h: time and impact speed

cards.back: The horizontal velocity $v_0\cos\theta$ (and the acceleration, $g$ down).

cards.front: Level-ground range, height, time of flight
Launch angle for maximum range (level ground)

cards.back: $\vec v_{AC} = \vec v_{AB} + \vec v_{BC}$, and $\vec v_{BA} = -\vec v_{AB}$.

cards.front: Fastest way across a river vs landing directly opposite
cards.back: Fastest: head straight across (time = width/speed). Opposite: head upstream at $\sin\alpha = v_{\text{current}}/v_{\text{boat}}$.
No net force means no change in velocity (constant speed in a straight line, or rest).
$\vec F_{\text{A on B}} = -\vec F_{\text{B on A}}$: equal, opposite, on different objects, same type of force.
Mass (kg) measures inertia and never changes; weight $mg$ (N) is the gravitational force and depends on $g$.
Isolate the object; draw weight; add a force for each contact (normal, friction, tension, push); choose axes along $\vec a$; write $\sum F = ma$ per axis.

cards.front: Scale reading in an elevator accelerating at a (up positive)

cards.back: $f_s \le \mu_s n$; equals $\mu_s n$ only on the verge of slipping.

cards.front: Weight components on an incline at θ
cards.back: $mg\sin\theta$ down the slope, $mg\cos\theta$ into the slope; $n = mg\cos\theta$.

cards.front: Acceleration sliding down an incline with friction
Angle at which an object just starts to slide
Block on table (μk) pulled by hanging mass $m_2$
Max speed on a flat curve
Minimum speed at the top of a vertical loop

cards.back: $W = Fd\cos\theta$ (θ between $\vec F$ and $\vec d$); zero if perpendicular, negative if opposing.
$K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f$ when only conservative forces do work.

cards.front: Speed after falling height h (any frictionless path)

cards.back: $F = -\dfrac{dU}{dx}$; equilibrium where $dU/dx = 0$, stable if $U$ is a minimum.
$P = W/\Delta t = Fv$; 1 W = 1 J/s; 1 hp = 746 W.

cards.front: Why do air bags and crumple zones help?
cards.back: They lengthen the stopping time, so the same $\Delta p$ needs a smaller average force.
When the net external force on the system is zero (component by component).
$\Delta v = u\ln(m_i/m_f)$, $u$ = exhaust speed relative to the rocket (no external force).
$u\,|dm/dt|$: exhaust speed times mass ejected per second.
$x_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{\sum m_ix_i}{M}$, or $\dfrac1M\int x\,dm$; $\vec F_{\text{ext}} = M\vec a_{\text{cm}}$.

cards.front: Elastic vs inelastic vs perfectly inelastic
cards.back: All conserve momentum. Elastic also conserves KE; perfectly inelastic objects stick and lose the most KE.
Momentum conservation for the collision, then energy conservation for the swing: $v = \dfrac{m + M}{m}\sqrt{2gh}$.
$s = r\theta$, $v = r\omega$, $a_t = r\alpha$, $a_c = r\omega^2$ (θ in radians).

cards.front: I for hoop, solid disk, solid sphere, hollow sphere (central axis)

cards.back: $\tau = rF\sin\theta = rF_\perp$; $\vec\tau = \vec r\times\vec F$; counterclockwise positive.

cards.front: Mass m hanging from a solid cylinder pulley of mass M
Speed at the bottom of a ramp for a rolling object with $I = cMR^2$

cards.back: Solid sphere, solid cylinder, hollow sphere, hoop (smallest $c$ first).
$L = I\omega$; particle: $L = mvr_\perp$; vector: $\vec L = \vec r\times\vec p$.
No external torque: $I_i\omega_i = I_f\omega_f$ (KE need not be conserved).

cards.front: Best pivot for an equilibrium torque equation
cards.back: A point where an unknown force acts, so it drops out.

cards.front: When does an object tip over?
cards.back: When its center of gravity moves beyond the edge of its base.
Stress $F/A$ = $Y$ × strain $\Delta L/L$, so $\Delta L = FL/(AY)$.
Shear: $F/A = S\,\Delta x/L$. Bulk: $\Delta P = -B\,\Delta V/V$.
Elliptical orbits (Sun at a focus); equal areas in equal times; $T^2 \propto a^3$.

cards.front: Period of a mass on a spring
Period of a simple pendulum (small angles)
SHM position, max speed, max acceleration
Does SHM period depend on amplitude?
cards.back: No (for ideal springs and small-angle pendulums).
Driving an oscillator at its natural frequency produces a large amplitude.
$m\ddot x + b\dot x + kx = 0$; write $\gamma = b/2m$, $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$.
$b = 2\sqrt{mk}$ ($\gamma = \omega_0$): fastest return to equilibrium with no overshoot. Overdamped is slower.
$Q = \omega_0/(2\gamma) = \sqrt{mk}/b$; amplitude falls by $e$ in about $Q/\pi$ cycles.

cards.front: Amplitude vs energy decay in a damped oscillator
cards.back: Amplitude $\propto e^{-bt/2m}$; energy $\propto e^{-bt/m}$ (twice as fast).

cards.front: Steady-state amplitude of a driven oscillator

cards.back: $A = F_0/(b\omega_0) = Q \times$ the static stretch $F_0/k$; displacement lags the force by $90^\circ$.
Half-power bandwidth $\Delta\omega = b/m$, so $Q = \omega_0/\Delta\omega$: high $Q$ means a tall, narrow peak.

cards.front: What changes when a wave enters a new medium?
cards.back: Speed and wavelength change; frequency stays the same.

cards.front: Average power of a wave on a string

cards.back: Transverse: medium moves ⊥ to travel (string). Longitudinal: medium moves ∥ (sound).

cards.front: Standing waves on a string fixed at both ends
Speed of sound in air at 20°C

cards.back: ×10 intensity: +10 dB. ×2 intensity: +3 dB. ×10 distance (point source): −20 dB.
$f' = f\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$; upper signs for motion toward.
$F_1/A_1 = F_2/A_2$; volumes moved are equal, so $A_1d_1 = A_2d_2$.
$P + \tfrac12\rho v^2 + \rho gy$ = constant along a streamline
$\Delta L = \alpha L\Delta T$; volume: $\Delta V = \beta V\Delta T$, $\beta \approx 3\alpha$
$\sum m c(T_f - T_i) = 0$ (add $\pm mL$ for phase changes)

cards.front: Average translational KE of a gas molecule
Internal energy of a monatomic ideal gas

cards.back: $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = Q - W$ ($Q$ in, $W$ by the gas)
$W = \int P\,dV$ = area under the PV curve; $P\Delta V$ at constant pressure.

cards.front: Monatomic ideal gas molar specific heats

cards.back: $e_C = 1 - T_C/T_H$ (kelvins); no engine between the same two reservoirs can do better.
The total entropy of an isolated system never decreases.

glossary.definition: The International System of Units, built on seven base units including the meter (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K) and mole (mol).
A unit built from base units by multiplying and dividing, such as the newton ($\text{kg·m/s}^2$) or joule ($\text{kg·m}^2/\text{s}^2$).
Writing a number as $a \times 10^n$ with $1 \le |a| < 10$; every digit of $a$ is significant.
A ratio equal to 1, such as $\tfrac{1000\text{ m}}{1\text{ km}}$, used to change units without changing the quantity.
The digits of a measured value that carry real information: all nonzero digits, zeros between them, and trailing zeros after a decimal point.
How close a measurement is to the true value.
How closely repeated measurements agree with each other, and how finely a value is stated.
The kind of physical quantity something is, written in brackets: length [L], mass [M], time [T]. Speed has dimension [L]/[T].
Checking or deriving relationships by requiring every term of an equation to have the same dimensions.
The power of ten closest to a value; used for quick estimates.
A quantity fully described by a number and a unit, with no direction (mass, time, energy, temperature).
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as displacement, velocity, force or momentum.
The vector sum of two or more vectors.
The projections of a vector onto the coordinate axes: $A_x = A\cos\theta$, $A_y = A\sin\theta$ for an angle measured from $+x$.
Vectors of length 1 that mark directions; $\hat\imath$, $\hat\jmath$, $\hat k$ point along $+x$, $+y$, $+z$.
$\vec A\cdot\vec B = AB\cos\phi = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z$, a scalar measuring how much two vectors point the same way.
$\vec A\times\vec B$, a vector of magnitude $AB\sin\phi$ perpendicular to both, with direction given by the right-hand rule.
Point the fingers of your right hand along the first vector, curl them toward the second; the thumb gives the direction of the cross product.
The description of motion (position, velocity, acceleration) without regard to its causes.
An object's coordinate relative to a chosen origin and positive direction.
Change in position, $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$ (a vector; can be negative or zero).
Total length of path traveled; always positive.
Displacement divided by elapsed time, $v_{\text{avg}} = \Delta x/\Delta t$.
Total distance divided by elapsed time.
The velocity at one instant, $v = dx/dt$: the slope of the position–time graph.
Rate of change of velocity, $a = dv/dt$, in m/s². It is a vector; its sign shows the direction of the change in velocity.
The free-fall acceleration near Earth's surface, $g \approx 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$ directed downward.
Motion under the influence of gravity alone, with acceleration $g$ downward regardless of mass.
The constant speed a falling object reaches when air drag balances its weight.
Two-dimensional motion under gravity alone: constant horizontal velocity plus free fall vertically, giving a parabolic path.
Horizontal distance a projectile travels; on level ground $R = v_0^2\sin 2\theta/g$.
The component of acceleration along the velocity; it changes the speed.
The component of acceleration perpendicular to the velocity, toward the center of curvature; it changes the direction of motion.
A set of coordinate axes attached to some object, from which positions and velocities are measured.
Velocity measured in a particular frame; $\vec v_{AC} = \vec v_{AB} + \vec v_{BC}$.
A reference frame that is not accelerating; Newton's laws hold in it.
A push or pull by one object on another; a vector measured in newtons (N).
SI unit of force: $1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg·m/s}^2$.
An object keeps a constant velocity (including rest) unless a net force acts on it.
The tendency of an object to keep its velocity; measured by its mass.
The vector sum of all forces acting on an object, $\sum\vec F$.
$\sum\vec F = m\vec a$, or generally $\vec F_{\text{net}} = d\vec p/dt$.
The measure of an object's inertia (resistance to acceleration), in kilograms; the same everywhere.
The state of zero net force (and, for extended objects, zero net torque): at rest or moving at constant velocity.
The gravitational force on an object, $W = mg$, directed downward.
The contact force a surface exerts perpendicular to itself; found from Newton's second law, not assumed equal to $mg$.
If A exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force on A. The pair acts on different objects.
A sketch of one object showing every force acting on it as an arrow; the starting point of a dynamics problem.
The normal force (scale reading) supporting an object; differs from $mg$ when the object accelerates vertically.
A contact force parallel to surfaces that opposes sliding or the tendency to slide.
Friction between sliding surfaces, $f_k = \mu_k n$, opposite to the sliding velocity.
The dimensionless ratio $\mu_k = f_k/n$ for a pair of sliding surfaces.
Friction between surfaces not sliding; adjusts to prevent motion up to $f_s = \mu_s n$.
The ratio $\mu_s = f_{s,\max}/n$; equals $\tan\theta$ at the angle where an object just starts to slide down an incline.
The pulling force a taut rope, string or cable exerts along its length.
An idealized rope with no mass, which therefore has the same tension throughout.
A massless, frictionless pulley that changes a rope's direction without changing its tension.
Two masses hung over a pulley; $a = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$.
Motion in a circle at constant speed; the acceleration $v^2/r$ points to the center.
The time for one complete cycle (revolution or oscillation), $T = 1/f$.
Number of cycles per second, $f = 1/T$, in hertz (Hz).
The center-directed acceleration of circular motion, $a_c = v^2/r = \omega^2 r$.
The net inward force required for circular motion, $mv^2/r$, supplied by real forces such as tension, friction, gravity or the normal force.
Energy transferred by a force acting through a displacement: $W = Fd\cos\theta$, or $\int\vec F\cdot d\vec\ell$. A scalar, in joules.
SI unit of work and energy: $1\text{ J} = 1\text{ N·m} = 1\text{ kg·m}^2/\text{s}^2$.
The total work done by all forces on an object; equals its change in kinetic energy.
Energy of motion, $K = \tfrac12mv^2 = p^2/(2m)$.
The net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K$.
An ideal spring exerts $F = -kx$, proportional to its stretch or compression and directed back toward equilibrium.
The stiffness $k$ of a spring in N/m: the force per unit stretch.
Stored energy of position or configuration associated with a conservative force; $W_{\text{cons}} = -\Delta U$.
A force whose work between two points is independent of the path (gravity, springs, electrostatic force).
Near Earth's surface, $U_g = mgy$ relative to a chosen zero level; in general $U = -GMm/r$.
Energy stored in a stretched or compressed spring, $U_s = \tfrac12kx^2$.
The sum of kinetic and potential energy, $E = K + U$.
If only conservative forces do work, $K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f$.
A force such as friction or drag whose work depends on the path; its work $W_{\text{nc}}$ changes the mechanical energy.
Rate of doing work or transferring energy: $P = W/\Delta t = \vec F\cdot\vec v$, in watts.
SI unit of power: $1\text{ W} = 1\text{ J/s}$. One horsepower is 746 W.
Ratio of useful output energy (or power) to input, $\eta = P_{\text{out}}/P_{\text{in}}$.
A position where $U(x) = E$, so the kinetic energy is zero and the particle reverses direction.
The product of mass and velocity, $\vec p = m\vec v$ (kg·m/s), a vector.
Force times the time it acts, $\vec J = \vec F_{\text{avg}}\Delta t = \int\vec F\,dt$, in N·s.
The impulse on an object equals its change in momentum: $\vec J = \Delta\vec p$.
The speed gained by a rocket with no external force, $\Delta v = u\ln(m_i/m_f)$, where $u$ is the exhaust speed relative to the rocket and $m_i/m_f$ the ratio of initial to final mass.
The forward force on a rocket from its exhaust, $u\,|dm/dt|$: exhaust speed relative to the rocket times the rate mass is ejected.
With zero net external force, a system's total momentum stays constant.
The mass-weighted average position, $x_{\text{cm}} = \sum m_ix_i/M$; it moves as if all external forces acted on the total mass there.
A collision in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
A collision in which momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not.
A collision in which the objects stick together; it loses the most kinetic energy allowed by momentum conservation.
Ratio of separation speed to approach speed in a collision: 1 for elastic, 0 for perfectly inelastic.
The angle subtending an arc equal to the radius: $\theta = s/r$. A full turn is $2\pi$ rad.
The change in angular position, $\Delta\theta$, in radians.
Rate of change of angle, $\omega = d\theta/dt$, in rad/s; $\omega = 2\pi f$.
Rate of change of angular velocity, $\alpha = d\omega/dt$, in rad/s².
Revolutions per minute; $1\text{ rpm} = 2\pi/60 \approx 0.1047$ rad/s.
Resistance to angular acceleration about an axis: $I = \sum m_ir_i^2 = \int r^2\,dm$ (kg·m²).
$I = I_{\text{cm}} + Md^2$ for an axis parallel to one through the center of mass, a distance $d$ away.
Kinetic energy of rotation, $K = \tfrac12I\omega^2$.
The turning effect of a force about an axis: $\tau = rF\sin\theta$, or $\vec\tau = \vec r\times\vec F$ (N·m).
The perpendicular distance from the axis to a force's line of action; $\tau = (\text{lever arm})\times F$.
Rolling in which the contact point is momentarily at rest, so $v_{\text{cm}} = R\omega$.
$L = I\omega$ for a rigid body about a fixed axis; in general $\vec L = \vec r\times\vec p$. Changed only by torque: $\vec\tau = d\vec L/dt$.
With zero net external torque, $L$ is constant: $I_i\omega_i = I_f\omega_f$.
A rapidly spinning wheel whose large angular momentum resists changes in direction; a torque makes it precess.
The slow rotation of a spinning object's axis caused by a torque perpendicular to its angular momentum; rate $\Omega = \tau/L$.
The state of a rigid body at rest with $\sum\vec F = 0$ and $\sum\tau = 0$.
The point where an object's total weight effectively acts; equals the center of mass in uniform gravity.
Force per unit area applied to a material, $F/A$, in pascals.
The fractional deformation of a material, such as $\Delta L/L$; dimensionless.
The ratio of tensile stress to strain for small deformations, $Y = (F/A)/(\Delta L/L)$; about $2\times10^{11}$ Pa for steel.
The largest stress a material can take and still return to its original shape when the load is removed.
The ratio of shear stress to shear strain, $S = (F/A)/(\Delta x/L)$, for a force applied parallel to a face; fluids have none.
The ratio of added pressure to fractional volume decrease, $B = -\Delta P/(\Delta V/V)$; a large $B$ means hard to compress.
Any two masses attract with $F = Gm_1m_2/r^2$ along the line joining them.
$G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², the constant in Newton's law of gravitation.
A dependence of the form $1/r^2$, as in gravity, Coulomb's law and the intensity of a point source.
An equatorial orbit with a 24-hour period (radius about $4.22\times10^7$ m), so the satellite stays above one point.
(1) Orbits are ellipses with the Sun at a focus; (2) equal areas in equal times; (3) $T^2 \propto a^3$.
Minimum launch speed to coast to infinity: $v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{2GM/R}$ (11.2 km/s for Earth).
Oscillation driven by a restoring force proportional to displacement, $F = -kx$; $x = A\cos(\omega t + \phi)$.
The maximum displacement from equilibrium in an oscillation or wave.
$\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi/T$ (rad/s); for a spring, $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$.
The angle $\phi$ in $x = A\cos(\omega t + \phi)$ that sets where the motion starts in its cycle.
A point mass on a light string; for small swings $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$, independent of mass and amplitude.
A rigid body swinging about a pivot a distance $d$ from its center of mass; $T = 2\pi\sqrt{I/(mgd)}$.
Loss of an oscillator's energy to friction or drag, making its amplitude decay.
Large-amplitude response when a system is driven at its natural frequency.
The constant $b$ (kg/s) in a velocity-proportional damping force $F = -bv$.
The angular frequency $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$ at which an oscillator vibrates when left alone with no damping.
Damping weaker than critical ($b < 2\sqrt{mk}$): the system still oscillates, at $\omega' = \sqrt{\omega_0^2 - \gamma^2}$, inside a decaying envelope $e^{-\gamma t}$, $\gamma = b/2m$.
Damping with $b = 2\sqrt{mk}$ ($\gamma = \omega_0$): the fastest return to equilibrium without overshooting.
Damping stronger than critical ($b > 2\sqrt{mk}$): the system returns to equilibrium without oscillating, more slowly than with critical damping.
A measure of how lightly damped an oscillator is: $Q = \omega_0/(2\gamma) = \sqrt{mk}/b$. It equals the resonant amplitude divided by the static stretch, and $\omega_0/\Delta\omega$.
A periodic external force, such as $F_0\cos\omega t$, that pushes an oscillator and feeds energy into it.
The angular frequency $\omega$ of the external force on a driven oscillator; the steady-state motion has this frequency.
The part of a driven oscillator's motion that dies away (as $e^{-\gamma t}$), leaving the steady state.
The lasting motion of a driven oscillator once transients have died out: $x = A\cos(\omega t - \delta)$ at the driving frequency.
The graph of a driven oscillator's steady-state amplitude (or absorbed power) against driving frequency; it peaks near $\omega_0$.
The width $\Delta\omega = b/m$ of a resonance, measured between the frequencies where the absorbed power is half its peak; $Q = \omega_0/\Delta\omega$.
A traveling disturbance that carries energy through a medium (or through space) without carrying matter along.
A wave that needs a material medium, such as sound or waves on a string.
A wave in which the medium moves perpendicular to the direction of travel.
A wave in which the medium moves parallel to the direction of travel, in compressions and rarefactions (e.g. sound).
The distance over which a wave repeats, crest to crest; $v = f\lambda$.
Mass per unit length of a string, $\mu = m/L$ (kg/m).
Where waves overlap, the net displacement is the sum of the individual displacements.
Overlap of waves in step, so their displacements add (path difference $m\lambda$).
Overlap of waves out of step, so their displacements cancel (path difference $(m + \tfrac12)\lambda$).
The difference in distance traveled by two waves to a point; it determines whether they interfere constructively or destructively.
A stationary oscillation pattern formed by two identical waves traveling in opposite directions.
A point in a standing wave that does not move; adjacent nodes are $\lambda/2$ apart.
A point of maximum oscillation in a standing wave, midway between nodes.
The allowed standing-wave frequencies of a system; for a string fixed at both ends, $f_n = nv/(2L)$.
The lowest standing-wave frequency of a system, $f_1$.
Power per unit area carried by a wave (W/m²); from a point source $I = P/(4\pi r^2)$.
$k = 2\pi/\lambda$ (rad/m), the spatial analog of angular frequency.
$\partial^2y/\partial x^2 = (1/v^2)\,\partial^2y/\partial t^2$, satisfied by any wave traveling at speed $v$.
The perceived highness or lowness of a sound, determined by its frequency.
Sound below about 20 Hz, too low for humans to hear.
Sound above about 20 kHz, too high for humans to hear; used in medical imaging and sonar.
$\beta = 10\log_{10}(I/I_0)$ in decibels, with $I_0 = 10^{-12}$ W/m².
Unit of sound intensity level; +10 dB is ten times the intensity, +3 dB about twice.
The rate at which loudness throbs when two close frequencies combine: $f_{\text{beat}} = |f_1 - f_2|$.
The change in observed frequency due to relative motion of source and observer: $f' = f\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$.
A cone of piled-up wavefronts from a source moving faster than the wave speed; half-angle $\sin\theta = v/v_s$.
Mass per unit volume, $\rho = m/V$ (kg/m³); water is 1000 kg/m³.
Perpendicular force per unit area, $P = F/A$, in pascals.
SI unit of pressure, $1\text{ Pa} = 1\text{ N/m}^2$; 1 atm $= 1.013\times10^5$ Pa.
Pressure above atmospheric, $P - P_{\text{atm}}$; what tire gauges read.
Total pressure including the atmosphere's contribution.
An instrument measuring atmospheric pressure, classically a mercury column ($P_{\text{atm}} = \rho gh$, 760 mm at sea level).
A pressure change applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished throughout it; basis of hydraulics, $F_1/A_1 = F_2/A_2$.
The net upward force a fluid exerts on an immersed object, equal to the weight of fluid displaced.
$F_B = \rho_{\text{fluid}}V_{\text{displaced}}\,g$.
A model fluid that is incompressible, nonviscous, and flows steadily without rotation.
The path followed by fluid elements in steady flow; streamlines never cross.
Volume passing a point per second, $Q = Av$ (m³/s).
$A_1v_1 = A_2v_2$ for an incompressible fluid: narrower sections flow faster.
Along a streamline of an ideal fluid, $P + \tfrac12\rho v^2 + \rho gy$ is constant.
At equal heights, faster-moving fluid has lower pressure.
Fluid leaves a hole a depth $h$ below the open surface at $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.
Internal friction in a fluid that resists flow between layers.
A measure of hotness tied to the average kinetic energy of particles; equal temperatures mean thermal equilibrium.
The state in which objects in contact no longer exchange net heat because they share the same temperature.
If A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with C, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
Temperature scale with water freezing at 0°C and boiling at 100°C (1 atm).
Temperature scale with $T_F = \tfrac95T_C + 32$.
The SI absolute temperature scale, $T = T_C + 273.15$; 0 K is absolute zero.
0 K ($-273.15$°C), the lowest possible temperature.
The fractional change in length per kelvin: $\Delta L = \alpha L\Delta T$.
Energy transferred because of a temperature difference (symbol $Q$, in joules).
Heat needed per kilogram per kelvin, $c$ in $Q = mc\Delta T$; 4186 J/(kg·K) for water.
Heat per kilogram absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature, $Q = mL$.
Latent heat for melting or freezing; $3.34\times10^5$ J/kg for water.
Latent heat for boiling or condensing; $2.26\times10^6$ J/kg for water.
Heat transfer through a material by molecular collisions; rate $kA\Delta T/L$.
Material property $k$ (W/(m·K)) setting how readily heat conducts through it.
Heat transfer by bulk motion of a fluid.
Heat transfer by electromagnetic waves; power $P = e\sigma AT^4$ (Stefan–Boltzmann law).
$dT/dt = -\kappa(T - T_s)$: an object approaches the surrounding temperature exponentially.
Amount of substance containing $N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}$ particles.
$N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}$ particles per mole.
$PV = nRT = Nk_BT$, with absolute pressure and temperature.
A gas of point particles that interact only through brief elastic collisions; real gases approach it at low pressure and high temperature.
Standard temperature and pressure: in this course 0°C (273.15 K) and 1 atm, where one mole of ideal gas occupies 22.4 L. (IUPAC now uses 1 bar = 100 kPa, giving 22.7 L.)
$v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\overline{v^2}} = \sqrt{3k_BT/m} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$.
Made of single atoms (He, Ne, Ar); an ideal monatomic gas has $E_{\text{int}} = \tfrac32nRT$.
Each quadratic degree of freedom of a molecule holds on average $\tfrac12k_BT$ of energy.
The distribution of molecular speeds in a gas at temperature $T$, peaked at $\sqrt{2k_BT/m}$ with a high-speed tail.
The total microscopic energy of a system's particles; for an ideal gas it depends only on $T$.
A graph of pressure versus volume; the area under a process curve is the work done by the gas.
$\Delta E_{\text{int}} = Q - W$, with $Q$ heat into the system and $W$ work done by it.
A property that depends only on the current state, not the path (internal energy, entropy, $P$, $V$, $T$).
At constant pressure; $W = P\Delta V$.
At constant volume; $W = 0$ and $Q = \Delta E_{\text{int}}$.
At constant temperature; for an ideal gas $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = 0$ and $Q = W = nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)$.
With no heat exchange ($Q = 0$); for an ideal gas $PV^\gamma$ is constant.
Heat per mole per kelvin; for a monatomic ideal gas $C_V = \tfrac32R$ and $C_P = \tfrac52R$.
A process that returns a system to its initial state, so $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = 0$ and net heat equals net work.
A cyclic device that absorbs heat $Q_H$, does work $W$, and rejects heat $Q_C$ to a colder reservoir.
$e = W/Q_H = 1 - Q_C/Q_H$ for a heat engine.
No cyclic engine converts heat entirely to work; heat does not flow spontaneously from cold to hot; total entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
An idealized process with no friction and only infinitesimal temperature differences, which can be run backward exactly.
The reversible cycle of two isotherms and two adiabats; its efficiency $1 - T_C/T_H$ is the maximum possible for any engine working between those two reservoir temperatures.
A device that uses work to move heat from a cold region to a warmer one.
For a refrigerator $K = Q_C/W$; for a heat pump $Q_H/W$. It can exceed 1.
A refrigerator used to deliver heat $Q_H$ to a warm space.
A state variable measuring disorder; $\Delta S = \int dQ_{\text{rev}}/T$, and $S = k_B\ln\Omega$.

references.title: Physical constants and data
references.body:
## Fundamental constants

| Quantity | Symbol | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Speed of light in vacuum | $c$ | $3.00\times10^8$ m/s |
| Gravitational constant | $G$ | $6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg² |
| Boltzmann's constant | $k_B$ | $1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K |
| Gas constant | $R$ | $8.314$ J/(mol·K) |
| Avogadro's number | $N_A$ | $6.022\times10^{23}$ mol⁻¹ |
| Atomic mass unit | u | $1.6605\times10^{-27}$ kg |
| Stefan–Boltzmann constant | $\sigma$ | $5.67\times10^{-8}$ W/(m²·K⁴) |

## Earth, Moon, Sun

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Free-fall acceleration at Earth's surface | $g = 9.8$ m/s² (9.81 at sea level) |
| Mass of Earth | $5.97\times10^{24}$ kg |
| Radius of Earth | $6.37\times10^6$ m |
| Mass of Moon | $7.35\times10^{22}$ kg |
| Radius of Moon | $1.74\times10^6$ m |
| $g$ on the Moon | 1.62 m/s² |
| Mass of Sun | $1.99\times10^{30}$ kg |
| Earth–Sun distance | $1.50\times10^{11}$ m |
| Atmospheric pressure (sea level) | $1.013\times10^5$ Pa |

## Material data

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Density of water | 1000 kg/m³ |
| Density of air (sea level, 20°C) | 1.20 kg/m³ |
| Speed of sound in air (20°C) | 343 m/s |
| Specific heat of water | 4186 J/(kg·K) |
| Specific heat of ice | 2100 J/(kg·K) |
| Latent heat of fusion of water | $3.34\times10^5$ J/kg |
| Latent heat of vaporization of water | $2.26\times10^6$ J/kg |

references.title: Mechanics equations
references.body:
## Vectors

| | |
|---|---|
| Components | $A_x = A\cos\theta$, $A_y = A\sin\theta$ |
| Magnitude, direction | $A = \sqrt{A_x^2 + A_y^2}$, $\tan\theta = A_y/A_x$ |
| Dot product | $\vec A\cdot\vec B = AB\cos\phi = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z$ |
| Cross product | $\lvert\vec A\times\vec B\rvert = AB\sin\phi$ (right-hand rule) |

## Kinematics

| | |
|---|---|
| Definitions | $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$, $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt}$; $\Delta x = \int v\,dt$ |
| Constant acceleration | $v = v_0 + at$; $\Delta x = v_0t + \tfrac12at^2$; $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2a\Delta x$; $\Delta x = \tfrac12(v_0 + v)t$ |
| Projectile (level ground) | $R = \dfrac{v_0^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$, $H = \dfrac{v_0^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$, $T = \dfrac{2v_0\sin\theta}{g}$ |
| Relative velocity | $\vec v_{AC} = \vec v_{AB} + \vec v_{BC}$ |
| Circular motion | $v = \dfrac{2\pi r}{T}$, $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{r} = \omega^2r$ |

## Forces

| | |
|---|---|
| Newton's second law | $\sum\vec F = m\vec a = \dfrac{d\vec p}{dt}$ |
| Weight | $W = mg$ |
| Friction | $f_k = \mu_kn$, $f_s \le \mu_sn$ |
| Incline | $mg\sin\theta$ along, $mg\cos\theta$ into the slope |
| Spring | $F = -kx$ |
| Centripetal | $\sum F_{\text{in}} = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$ |
| Atwood machine | $a = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$ |

## Energy and momentum

| | |
|---|---|
| Work | $W = Fd\cos\theta = \int\vec F\cdot d\vec\ell$ |
| Kinetic energy | $K = \tfrac12mv^2$; $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K$ |
| Potential energy | $U_g = mgy$, $U_s = \tfrac12kx^2$, $F = -\dfrac{dU}{dx}$ |
| Energy conservation | $K_i + U_i + W_{\text{nc}} = K_f + U_f$ |
| Power | $P = \dfrac{W}{t} = Fv$ |
| Momentum, impulse | $\vec p = m\vec v$; $\vec J = \int\vec F\,dt = \Delta\vec p$ |
| Center of mass | $x_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{\sum m_ix_i}{M} = \dfrac1M\int x\,dm$ |
| Elastic collision (target at rest) | $v_{1f} = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i}$, $v_{2f} = \dfrac{2m_1}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i}$ |
| Perfectly inelastic | $v_f = \dfrac{m_1v_1 + m_2v_2}{m_1 + m_2}$ |
| Rocket (no external force) | $\Delta v = u\ln\dfrac{m_i}{m_f}$; thrust $= u\,\lvert dm/dt\rvert$ |

## Rotation

| Linear | Rotational |
|---|---|
| $x$, $v$, $a$ | $\theta$, $\omega$, $\alpha$; $v = r\omega$, $a_t = r\alpha$ |
| $m$ | $I = \sum mr^2 = \int r^2\,dm$; $I = I_{\text{cm}} + Md^2$ |
| $F = ma$ | $\tau = rF\sin\theta = I\alpha$; $\vec\tau = \vec r\times\vec F$ |
| $K = \tfrac12mv^2$ | $K = \tfrac12I\omega^2$ |
| $p = mv$ | $L = I\omega$; $\vec L = \vec r\times\vec p$; $\tau = dL/dt$ |
| $P = Fv$ | $P = \tau\omega$ |

| Shape (mass $M$) | $I$ |
|---|---|
| Hoop, radius $R$ | $MR^2$ |
| Solid disk or cylinder | $\tfrac12MR^2$ |
| Solid sphere | $\tfrac25MR^2$ |
| Thin spherical shell | $\tfrac23MR^2$ |
| Rod about center / end | $\tfrac1{12}ML^2$ / $\tfrac13ML^2$ |

Rolling from height $h$ ($I = cMR^2$): $v = \sqrt{2gh/(1 + c)}$. Static equilibrium: $\sum\vec F = 0$, $\sum\tau = 0$.

## Elasticity

| | |
|---|---|
| Tension or compression | $\dfrac{F}{A} = Y\dfrac{\Delta L}{L}$, so $\Delta L = \dfrac{FL}{AY}$ (steel $Y \approx 2\times10^{11}$ Pa, aluminum $7\times10^{10}$ Pa) |
| Shear | $\dfrac{F}{A} = S\dfrac{\Delta x}{L}$ |
| Bulk (volume) | $\Delta P = -B\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}$ |

## Gravitation

| | |
|---|---|
| Universal gravitation | $F = \dfrac{Gm_1m_2}{r^2}$; $g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$ |
| Circular orbit | $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$, $T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{GM}r^3$ |
| Potential energy | $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}$ |
| Escape speed | $v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$ |

references.title: Units and conversions
references.body:
## SI prefixes

| Prefix | Symbol | Factor | Prefix | Symbol | Factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tera | T | $10^{12}$ | centi | c | $10^{-2}$ |
| giga | G | $10^{9}$ | milli | m | $10^{-3}$ |
| mega | M | $10^{6}$ | micro | μ | $10^{-6}$ |
| kilo | k | $10^{3}$ | nano | n | $10^{-9}$ |
| | | | pico | p | $10^{-12}$ |

## Derived SI units

| Quantity | Unit | In base units |
|---|---|---|
| Force | newton (N) | kg·m/s² |
| Energy, work | joule (J) | N·m = kg·m²/s² |
| Power | watt (W) | J/s |
| Pressure | pascal (Pa) | N/m² |
| Frequency | hertz (Hz) | s⁻¹ |

## Common conversions

| From | To |
|---|---|
| 1 km/h | 0.2778 m/s (divide by 3.6) |
| 1 mi/h | 0.447 m/s |
| 1 cm² | $10^{-4}$ m² |
| 1 cm³ (1 mL) | $10^{-6}$ m³ |
| 1 L | $10^{-3}$ m³ |
| 1 atm | $1.013\times10^5$ Pa = 760 mm Hg = 14.7 lb/in² |
| 1 kWh | $3.6\times10^6$ J |
| 1 cal | 4.186 J (1 food Calorie = 1000 cal) |
| 1 hp | 746 W |
| 1 rev | $2\pi$ rad = 360° |
| 1 rpm | $2\pi/60 = 0.1047$ rad/s |
| 1 u | $1.6605\times10^{-27}$ kg |
| 1 year | $3.16\times10^7$ s |

## Temperature

| Conversion | Formula |
|---|---|
| Celsius to kelvin | $T = T_C + 273.15$ |
| Celsius to Fahrenheit | $T_F = \tfrac95T_C + 32$ |
| Temperature differences | 1 K = 1°C = 1.8°F |

## Significant figures

| Operation | Keep |
|---|---|
| Multiply or divide | fewest significant figures among the inputs |
| Add or subtract | fewest decimal places among the inputs |
| Exact numbers (counts, defined conversions) | don't limit precision |

references.title: Oscillations, waves, fluids, and thermodynamics
references.body:
## Oscillations

| | |
|---|---|
| SHM | $x = A\cos(\omega t + \phi)$; $\ddot x = -\omega^2x$ |
| Spring | $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ |
| Simple pendulum | $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$ |
| Physical pendulum | $T = 2\pi\sqrt{I/(mgd)}$ |
| Maxima | $v_{\max} = A\omega$, $a_{\max} = A\omega^2$; $E = \tfrac12kA^2$ |
| Damped ($\gamma = b/2m$) | $m\ddot x + b\dot x + kx = 0$; underdamped $x = A_0e^{-\gamma t}\cos(\omega' t + \phi)$, $\omega' = \sqrt{\omega_0^2 - \gamma^2}$; critical $b = 2\sqrt{mk}$ |
| Quality factor | $Q = \dfrac{\omega_0}{2\gamma} = \dfrac{\sqrt{mk}}{b} = \dfrac{\omega_0}{\Delta\omega}$, bandwidth $\Delta\omega = b/m$ |
| Driven ($F_0\cos\omega t$) | $A = \dfrac{F_0/m}{\sqrt{(\omega_0^2 - \omega^2)^2 + (2\gamma\omega)^2}}$; at $\omega_0$: $A = \dfrac{F_0}{b\omega_0} = Q\dfrac{F_0}{k}$ |

## Waves and sound

| | |
|---|---|
| Wave speed | $v = f\lambda$; string: $v = \sqrt{F_T/\mu}$ |
| Traveling wave | $y = A\sin(kx - \omega t)$, $k = 2\pi/\lambda$, $\omega = 2\pi f$ |
| Power on a string | $P_{\text{avg}} = \tfrac12\mu A^2\omega^2v$ |
| String fixed at both ends; open pipe | $f_n = \dfrac{nv}{2L}$, $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ |
| Pipe closed at one end | $f_n = \dfrac{nv}{4L}$, $n = 1, 3, 5, \ldots$ |
| Intensity | $I = \dfrac{P}{4\pi r^2}$; $\beta = 10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_0}$, $I_0 = 10^{-12}$ W/m² |
| Beats | $f_{\text{beat}} = \lvert f_1 - f_2\rvert$ |
| Doppler | $f' = f\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$ (upper signs: approaching) |

## Fluids

| | |
|---|---|
| Density, pressure | $\rho = m/V$, $P = F/A$ |
| Depth | $P = P_0 + \rho gh$; $dP/dy = -\rho g$ |
| Pascal | $F_1/A_1 = F_2/A_2$ |
| Buoyancy | $F_B = \rho_{\text{fluid}}V_{\text{disp}}g$ |
| Continuity | $A_1v_1 = A_2v_2$ |
| Bernoulli | $P + \tfrac12\rho v^2 + \rho gy$ = const |
| Torricelli | $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ |

## Heat and gases

| | |
|---|---|
| Expansion | $\Delta L = \alpha L\Delta T$ |
| Heat | $Q = mc\Delta T$; phase change $Q = mL$ |
| Conduction, radiation | $Q/t = kA\Delta T/L$; $P = e\sigma AT^4$ |
| Ideal gas | $PV = nRT = Nk_BT$ |
| Kinetic theory | $\tfrac12m\overline{v^2} = \tfrac32k_BT$; $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ |
| Monatomic gas | $E_{\text{int}} = \tfrac32nRT$; $C_V = \tfrac32R$, $C_P = \tfrac52R$, $\gamma = \tfrac53$ |

## Thermodynamics

| | |
|---|---|
| First law | $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = Q - W$ ($W$ by the gas) |
| Work by gas | $W = \int P\,dV$; isobaric $P\Delta V$; isothermal $nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)$ |
| Adiabatic | $PV^\gamma$ = const, $TV^{\gamma - 1}$ = const |
| Engine | $e = \dfrac{W}{Q_H} = 1 - \dfrac{Q_C}{Q_H}$; Carnot $e = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$ |
| Refrigerator | $K = Q_C/W$; Carnot $\dfrac{T_C}{T_H - T_C}$ |
| Entropy | $\Delta S = \int\dfrac{dQ_{\text{rev}}}{T}$; $Q/T$ at constant $T$; heating at constant $c$: $mc\ln(T_2/T_1)$ |

drills.title: Convert km/h to m/s
drills.prompt: A car travels at {v} km/h. Express this speed in m/s (3 significant figures).
drills.solution:
$${v}\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}} \times \frac{1000\text{ m}}{1\text{ km}} \times \frac{1\text{ h}}{3600\text{ s}} = \frac{{v}}{3.6}\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$

So the speed is **{ms:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Convert an area from cm² to m²
drills.prompt: A solar cell has an area of {a} cm². What is its area in m²? (The conversion is exact, so give every digit.)
drills.solution:
$1\text{ cm} = 10^{-2}\text{ m}$, so $1\text{ cm}^2 = 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2$ (square the factor).

${a:dp0}\text{ cm}^2 \times 10^{-4}\,\tfrac{\text{m}^2}{\text{cm}^2} =$ **{m2:num4} m²**.

drills.title: Area with significant figures
drills.prompt: A rectangular sheet measures {l} m by {w} m. Find its area, rounded to the correct number of significant figures.
drills.solution: ${l} \times {w} = {A:num4}\text{ m}^2$. For a product, keep the fewest significant figures among the inputs: {l} has 3 and {w} has 2, so round to 2 significant figures: **{A:sig2} m²**.

drills.title: Components of a vector
drills.prompt: A force of {A} N points at {th}° measured counterclockwise from the $+x$ axis. Find its $x$ and $y$ components (include the signs), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$F_x = F\cos\theta = {A}\cos {th}^\circ =$ **{Ax:sig3} N**

$F_y = F\sin\theta = {A}\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{Ay:sig3} N**

The signs come out of the trig functions automatically when the angle is measured from $+x$.

drills.title: Add two displacement vectors
drills.prompt: A drone flies {a} km at {t1}° (counterclockwise from east), then {b} km at {t2}°. Find the magnitude of its total displacement and its direction in degrees counterclockwise from east (magnitude to 3 significant figures, direction to the nearest 0.1°).
drills.solution:
$R_x = {a}\cos {t1}^\circ + {b}\cos {t2}^\circ = {Rx:num2}$ km

$R_y = {a}\sin {t1}^\circ + {b}\sin {t2}^\circ = {Ry:num2}$ km

$R = \sqrt{R_x^2 + R_y^2} =$ **{R:sig3} km**, at $\theta =$ **{th:num1}°** (check the quadrant from the signs of $R_x$ and $R_y$).

drills.title: Angle between two vectors
drills.prompt: For $\vec A = {a1}\hat\imath {a2:signed}\hat\jmath {a3:signed}\hat k$ and $\vec B = {b1}\hat\imath {b2:signed}\hat\jmath {b3:signed}\hat k$, find $\vec A\cdot\vec B$ and the angle between the vectors in degrees (to the nearest 0.1°).

drills.title: Average velocity and average speed
drills.prompt: A jogger runs {d1} m east in {t1} s, then turns and runs {d2} m west in {t2} s. Find her average velocity (east positive) and her average speed for the whole run, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Displacement: $\Delta x = {d1} - {d2} = {dx}$ m; total time $\Delta t = {t1} + {t2} = {tt}$ s.

Average velocity $= \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} =$ **{vavg:sig3} m/s** (east).

Distance $= {d1} + {d2}$ m, so average speed $=$ **{savg:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Velocity and acceleration from x(t)
drills.prompt: A particle moves along $x$ with $x(t) = {a:coef}t^3 {b:signedcoef}t^2 {c:signedcoef}t$ (meters, seconds). Find its velocity and acceleration at $t = {t}$ s (exact values).
drills.solution:
$v(t) = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = {a3}t^2 {b2:signed}t {c:signed}$, so $v({t}) =$ **{v} m/s**.

$a(t) = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = {a6}t {b2:signed}$, so $a({t}) =$ **{acc} m/s²**.

drills.title: Braking distance and time
drills.prompt: A car moving at {v0} m/s brakes with a constant acceleration of magnitude {dec} m/s². How far does it travel while stopping, and how long does it take? Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
With $v = 0$ and $a = -{dec}$ m/s²: $0 = v_0^2 - 2({dec})\Delta x$, so $\Delta x = \dfrac{{v0}^2}{2({dec})} =$ **{d:sig3} m**.

$0 = {v0} - {dec}\,t$, so $t =$ **{t:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Time and speed of a dropped object
drills.prompt: A wrench is dropped from rest from a height of {h} m. Ignoring air resistance and using $g = 9.8$ m/s², how long does it fall, and how fast is it moving at the ground? Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$h = \tfrac12 g t^2 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{2({h})/9.8} =$ **{t:sig3} s**.

$v = gt = 9.8({t:sig3}) =$ **{v:sig3} m/s** (also $v = \sqrt{2gh}$).

drills.title: Ball thrown straight up
drills.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up at {v0} m/s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its maximum height above the launch point and its total time in the air (until it returns to the launch height), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
At the top $v_y = 0$: $0 = {v0}^2 - 2(9.8)H$, so $H =$ **{H:sig3} m**.

Time up $= {v0}/9.8$ s; time down is the same, so $T = 2({v0})/9.8 =$ **{T:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Horizontal launch from a height
drills.prompt: A ball leaves the edge of a {h} m high ledge moving horizontally at {v} m/s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², how far from the base of the ledge does it land, and what is its speed just before landing? Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Fall time from the vertical motion: $t = \sqrt{2h/g} = \sqrt{2({h})/9.8} = {t:sig3}$ s.

Horizontal distance: $x = v t = {v}({t:sig3}) =$ **{x:sig3} m**.

At impact $v_y = gt = {vy:num2}$ m/s, so speed $= \sqrt{{v}^2 + {vy:num2}^2} =$ **{s:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Range, height and flight time on level ground
drills.prompt: A ball is launched from level ground at {v0} m/s, {th}° above horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the time of flight, the maximum height and the range, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v_{0x} = {v0}\cos {th}^\circ = {vx:num2}$ m/s, $v_{0y} = {v0}\sin {th}^\circ = {vy:num2}$ m/s.

$T = 2v_{0y}/g =$ **{T:sig3} s**; $H = v_{0y}^2/(2g) =$ **{H:sig3} m**; $R = v_{0x}T = \dfrac{v_0^2\sin 2\theta}{g} =$ **{R:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Crossing a river
drills.prompt: A river {w} m wide flows at {vc} m/s. A boat moves at {vs} m/s relative to the water. (a) Heading straight across, how far downstream does it land? (b) To land directly opposite, how many degrees upstream from straight across must it head? Give the drift to 3 significant figures and the angle to the nearest 0.1°.
drills.solution:
(a) Crossing time uses only the across component: $t = {w}/{vs} = {t:num2}$ s. Drift $= {vc} \times {t:num2} =$ **{drift:sig3} m**.

(b) The upstream component must cancel the current: ${vs}\sin\alpha = {vc}$, so $\alpha = \sin^{-1}({vc}/{vs}) =$ **{ang:num1}°**.

drills.title: Airplane in a crosswind
drills.prompt: A plane with airspeed {va} km/h must fly due north while a wind blows toward the east at {vw} km/h. How many degrees west of north must it head, and what is its ground speed? Give the heading to the nearest 0.1° and the ground speed to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\vec v_{PG} = \vec v_{PA} + \vec v_{AG}$. The plane's eastward airspeed component must be $-{vw}$ km/h: ${va}\sin\alpha = {vw}$, so $\alpha =$ **{head:num1}°** west of north.

Ground speed $= {va}\cos\alpha = \sqrt{{va}^2 - {vw}^2} =$ **{vg:sig3} km/h**.

drills.title: Velocity and speed from a position vector
drills.prompt: A particle's position is $\vec r(t) = ({a:coef}t^2)\,\hat\imath + ({b}t - {c:coef}t^3)\,\hat\jmath$ in meters. Find $v_x$ and $v_y$ (exact values) and the speed (to 3 significant figures) at $t = {t}$ s.
drills.solution:
$\vec v = \dfrac{d\vec r}{dt} = ({a2}t)\,\hat\imath + ({b} - {c3}t^2)\,\hat\jmath$.

At $t = {t}$: $v_x =$ **{vx} m/s**, $v_y =$ **{vy} m/s**, speed $= \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} =$ **{sp:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Acceleration with an angled pull
drills.prompt: A {m} kg sled on frictionless ice is pulled by a rope with tension {F} N at {th}° above horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the sled's acceleration and the normal force on it. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Horizontal: ${F}\cos {th}^\circ = {m}a$, so $a =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

Vertical ($a_y = 0$): $n + {F}\sin {th}^\circ - {m}(9.8) = 0$, so $n =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Apparent weight in an elevator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg person stands on a scale in an elevator accelerating {dir} at {acc} m/s². What does the scale read? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s². Give the answer to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The scale reads the normal force. With up positive, $n - mg = ma$, where $a = +{acc}$ m/s² if the acceleration is upward and $-{acc}$ m/s² if downward.

Acceleration is {dir}, so $a = {sa}$ m/s² and $n = m(g + a) = {m}(9.8 + ({sa})) =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Net force from two perpendicular forces
drills.prompt: Two horizontal forces act on a {m} kg puck on frictionless ice: {F1} N east and {F2} N north. Find the magnitude of its acceleration and its direction in degrees north of east. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{{F1}^2 + {F2}^2} = {Fn:num2}$ N, so $a = F_{\text{net}}/m = {Fn:num2}/{m} =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

Direction: $\tan^{-1}({F2}/{F1}) =$ **{ang:sig3}°** north of east (the acceleration points along the net force).

drills.title: Block on a frictionless incline
drills.prompt: A block is released from rest on a frictionless ramp inclined at {th}°. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its acceleration and its speed after sliding {L} m along the ramp. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Along the slope only $mg\sin\theta$ acts: $a = g\sin\theta = 9.8\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$v^2 = 2aL$, so $v = \sqrt{2({a:num2})({L})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Sliding down an incline with friction
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block slides down a {th}° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is {mu}. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the friction force and the block's acceleration. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$n = mg\cos\theta = {m}(9.8)\cos {th}^\circ$, so $f_k = \mu_k n =$ **{f:sig3} N** (up the slope).

$a = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta) = 9.8(\sin {th}^\circ - {mu}\cos {th}^\circ) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²** down the slope.

drills.title: Force needed to start a box moving
drills.prompt: A {m} kg box rests on a level floor with $\mu_s = {ms}$ and $\mu_k = {mk}$. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the smallest horizontal force that starts it moving, and its acceleration if that same force keeps pushing once it slides. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$n = mg = {m}(9.8)$ N. Maximum static friction: $\mu_s n =$ **{Fs:sig3} N**, the force needed to start it.

Sliding: $f_k = \mu_k n$, so $a = \dfrac{\mu_s n - \mu_k n}{\,m} = (\mu_s - \mu_k)g =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

drills.title: Atwood machine
drills.prompt: Masses of {m1} kg and {m2} kg hang on either side of an ideal pulley. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the magnitude of their acceleration and the tension in the rope. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Heavier side down: ${m1}g - T = {m1}a$ and $T - {m2}g = {m2}a$. Adding:

$a = \dfrac{{m1} - {m2}}{{m1} + {m2}}(9.8) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = {m2}(g + a) = \dfrac{2m_1m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Block on a table pulled by a hanging mass
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg block on a horizontal table ($\mu_k = {mu}$) is tied by a rope over an ideal pulley to a hanging {m2} kg mass. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the acceleration and the tension. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Table block: $T - \mu_k m_1 g = m_1 a$. Hanging mass: $m_2 g - T = m_2 a$. Adding:

$a = \dfrac{m_2 - \mu_k m_1}{m_1 + m_2}g = \dfrac{{m2} - ({mu})({m1})}{{m1} + {m2}}(9.8) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = m_2(g - a) =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Tension in two symmetric cables
drills.prompt: A {m} kg sign hangs at rest from two cables, each making {th}° with the horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the tension in each cable. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Horizontal components cancel by symmetry. Vertically, $2T\sin\theta = mg$:

$T = \dfrac{{m}(9.8)}{2\sin {th}^\circ} =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Centripetal acceleration and force
drills.prompt: A {m} kg ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle of radius {r} m on a frictionless table, completing one revolution every {T} s. Find its speed, its centripetal acceleration and the string tension. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v = 2\pi r/T = 2\pi({r})/{T} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$a_c = v^2/r =$ **{ac:sig3} m/s²**, toward the center.

The string supplies the inward force: $T_{\text{string}} = ma_c =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Maximum speed on a flat curve
drills.prompt: What is the maximum speed at which a car can round a flat curve of radius {r} m if the coefficient of static friction between tires and road is {mu}? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² and answer in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Static friction supplies the inward force: $\mu_s mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{\,r}$, so

$v = \sqrt{\mu_s g r} = \sqrt{({mu})(9.8)({r})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s** (about {kmh:num1} km/h). The mass cancels.

drills.title: Vertical loop
drills.prompt: A roller coaster loop has radius {r} m. (a) What minimum speed must a car have at the top to stay on the track? (b) A {m} kg rider passes the bottom at {vb} m/s; what normal force does the seat exert on her there? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s². Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) At the limit $n = 0$ and gravity alone gives the inward force: $mg = mv^2/r$, so $v_{\min} = \sqrt{gr} =$ **{vmin:sig3} m/s**.

(b) At the bottom the net force is upward: $n - mg = mv^2/r$, so $n = {m}(9.8) + \dfrac{{m}({vb})^2}{{r}} =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Work done by an angled force and by friction
drills.prompt: A crate is dragged {d} m across a level floor by a rope with tension {F} N at {th}° above horizontal. Kinetic friction on the crate is {f} N. Find the work done by the rope, the work done by friction (with its sign), and the net work, in joules to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Rope: $W = Fd\cos\theta = {F}({d})\cos {th}^\circ =$ **{WF:sig3} J**.

Friction opposes the motion ($\theta = 180^\circ$): $W = -{f}({d}) =$ **{Wf} J**.

Gravity and the normal force are perpendicular to the motion and do no work, so $W_{\text{net}} =$ **{Wnet:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Work–energy theorem
drills.prompt: A {m} kg cart moving at {v0} m/s is pushed {d} m by a constant net force of {F} N in its direction of motion. Use the work–energy theorem to find its final speed in m/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$W_{\text{net}} = Fd = {F}({d}) = {W:dp0}$ J $= \tfrac12mv_f^2 - \tfrac12mv_i^2$.

$v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + 2W/m} = \sqrt{{v0}^2 + 2({W:dp0})/{m}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Spring force and stored energy
drills.prompt: A spring with spring constant {k} N/m is stretched {xcm} cm from its natural length. What force does it exert (N), and how much work (J) was needed to stretch it? Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Hooke's law: $|F| = kx = {k:dp0}({x}) =$ **{F:sig3} N** (pulling back toward equilibrium).

Work = area under the $F$–$x$ line $= \tfrac12kx^2 = \tfrac12({k:dp0})({x})^2 =$ **{U:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Speed at the bottom of a ramp (with and without friction)
drills.prompt: A {m} kg box starts from rest at the top of a ramp {h} m high. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find (a) its speed at the bottom if the ramp is frictionless, and (b) its speed if friction removes {pct}% of its initial potential energy. Give speeds in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) $mgh = \tfrac12mv^2$, so $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({h})} =$ **{v0:sig3} m/s**.

(b) Friction removes {pct}% of $mgh$, so $\tfrac12mv^2 = (1 - {pct}/100)\,mgh$ and $v =$ **{v1:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Spring launcher
drills.prompt: A spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m is compressed {xcm} cm and launches a {mg} g ball straight up. Ignoring air resistance and using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the ball's speed as it leaves the spring (neglect the small height change during launch) and the maximum height it reaches above the release point. Give the speed in m/s and the height in m, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Stored energy: $\tfrac12kx^2 = \tfrac12({k:dp0})({x})^2 = {U:num4}$ J.

Launch speed: $\tfrac12mv^2 = {U:num4}$ J with $m = {m}$ kg, so $v =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

Max height: $mgh = {U:num4}$ J, so $h = \dfrac{{U:num4}}{({m})(9.8)} =$ **{h:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Power to lift a load
drills.prompt: A motor lifts a {m} kg load {h} m at constant speed in {t} s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the power delivered to the load and, if the motor is {eff}% efficient, the electrical power it draws, in watts to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Work against gravity: $mgh = {m:dp0}(9.8)({h})$ J. $P = \dfrac{mgh}{\,t} =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

Input: $P_{\text{in}} = P/\eta = P/{eff}\% =$ **{Pin:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Impulse and average force in a rebound
drills.prompt: A {mg} g ball hits a wall at {v1} m/s and rebounds straight back at {v2} m/s. The contact lasts {tms} ms. Find the magnitude of the impulse (N·s) and of the average force on the ball (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Rebound direction positive: $\Delta p = m(v_f - v_i) = {m}({v2} - (-{v1})) =$ **{J:sig3} N·s**.

$F_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{{J:num4}}{{tms}\times10^{-3}} =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Recoil (momentum from rest)
drills.prompt: A {M} kg person standing on frictionless ice throws a {m} kg package horizontally at {v} m/s. With what speed does the person recoil? Give m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: ${m}({v}) + {M}V = 0$.

$|V| = \dfrac{{m}({v})}{{M}} =$ **{V:sig3} m/s**, opposite to the throw.

drills.title: Center of mass of three particles
drills.prompt: Find the center of mass of {m1} kg at $({x1}, {y1})$, {m2} kg at $({x2}, {y2})$ and {m3} kg at $({x3}, {y3})$ (coordinates in meters). Give each coordinate in meters to 2 decimal places.

drills.title: Perfectly inelastic collision
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg car moving at {v1} m/s collides with a {m2} kg car moving at {v2} m/s along the same line (negative means the opposite direction), and they lock together. Find their common velocity (m/s, with sign) and the kinetic energy lost (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Momentum: ${m1:dp0}({v1}) + {m2:dp0}({v2}) = ({m1:dp0} + {m2:dp0})v_f$, so $v_f =$ **{vf:sig3} m/s**.

$K_i = {Ki:dp0}$ J and $K_f = \tfrac12({Mt:dp0})v_f^2 = {Kf:dp0}$ J, so the loss is $K_i - K_f =$ **{dK:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Elastic collision with a target at rest
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg cart moving at {v} m/s collides head-on and elastically with a {m2} kg cart at rest. Find both final velocities in m/s, to 3 significant figures (positive = original direction of motion).
drills.solution:
$v_{1f} = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} = \dfrac{{m1} - {m2}}{{m1} + {m2}}({v}) =$ **{v1f:sig3} m/s**

$v_{2f} = \dfrac{2m_1}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} =$ **{v2f:sig3} m/s**

Check: they separate at $v_{2f} - v_{1f} = \dfrac{2m_1 - (m_1 - m_2)}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} = v_{1i} = {v}$ m/s, the same as the approach speed.

drills.title: Ballistic pendulum
drills.prompt: A {mg} g bullet embeds itself in a {M} kg block hanging from strings. The block swings up {hcm} cm. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the block's speed just after impact and the bullet's initial speed, in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Swing (energy conserved): $V = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({hcm}/100)} =$ **{V:sig3} m/s**.

Collision (momentum conserved): $mv = (m + M)V$, so $v = \dfrac{{m:dp3} + {M}}{{m:dp3}}({V:num4}) =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: The rocket equation and thrust
drills.prompt: A rocket of initial mass {mi} t (1 t = 1000 kg) in deep space ejects exhaust at {u} km/s relative to the rocket, at a rate of {R:dp0} kg/s, until it has burned fuel equal to {pct}% of its initial mass. Find its thrust (N), how long the burn lasts (s), and the speed it gains (km/s), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Thrust $= u\,|dm/dt| = ({u}\times10^{3})({R:dp0}) = \mathbf{{thrust:texsci}}$ N.

The final mass is $m_f = {mi}(1 - {pct}/100) = {mf:sig4}$ t, so the burn uses ${mi} - {mf:sig4}$ t of fuel and lasts **{tb:sig3} s** at {R:dp0} kg/s.

$\Delta v = u\ln\dfrac{m_i}{m_f} = {u}\ln\dfrac{{mi}}{{mf:sig4}} =$ **{dv:sig3} km/s**.

drills.title: Spinning down with constant angular acceleration
drills.prompt: A wheel spinning at {rpm} rpm slows uniformly to rest in {t} s. Find its angular acceleration (rad/s², with sign) and the number of revolutions it makes while stopping, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = {rpm:dp0}\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = {w0:num2}$ rad/s.

$\alpha = \dfrac{0 - \omega_0}{\,t} =$ **{alpha:sig3} rad/s²**.

$\Delta\theta = \tfrac12(\omega_0 + 0)t = {th:dp1}$ rad $=$ **{rev:sig3} rev**.

drills.title: Moment of inertia of masses on a rod
drills.prompt: A uniform rod of mass {M} kg and length {L} m has a small {m1} kg mass at its left end and a {m2} kg mass at its right end. Find the moment of inertia about (a) a perpendicular axis through the rod's center and (b) a perpendicular axis through the left end. Give kg·m² to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) Rod: $\tfrac1{12}ML^2$; each end mass is $L/2$ away: $I = \tfrac1{12}({M})({L})^2 + ({m1} + {m2})({L}/2)^2 =$ **{Ic:sig3} kg·m²**.

(b) Rod about an end: $\tfrac13ML^2$; the left mass is on the axis, the right mass is $L$ away: $I = \tfrac13({M})({L})^2 + {m2}({L})^2 =$ **{Ie:sig3} kg·m²**.

drills.title: Rotational kinetic energy of a disk
drills.prompt: A {M} kg {shape} of radius {R} m spins about its central axis at {rpm} rpm. Find its moment of inertia (kg·m²) and its rotational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
For a {shape}, $I = cMR^2$ with $c = {shape:num1}$, so $I =$ **{I:sig3} kg·m²**.

$\omega = {rpm:dp0}\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = {w:num2}$ rad/s, so $K = \tfrac12I\omega^2 =$ **{K:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Torque from an angled force
drills.prompt: A force of {F} N is applied at the end of a {r} m wrench, making an angle of {th}° with the handle. Find the torque about the bolt, and the maximum torque that force could produce, in N·m to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\tau = rF\sin\theta = ({r})({F})\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{tau:sig3} N·m**.

The maximum occurs for a perpendicular push: $rF =$ **{tmax:sig3} N·m**.

drills.title: Mass hanging from a heavy pulley
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block hangs from a light rope wrapped around a {M} kg solid cylinder of radius {R} m that turns freely on a frictionless axle. The block is released. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the block's acceleration (m/s²), the rope tension (N) and the cylinder's angular acceleration (rad/s²), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Block: $mg - T = ma$. Cylinder: $TR = \tfrac12MR^2\alpha$ with $\alpha = a/R$, so $T = \tfrac12Ma$.

$a = \dfrac{mg}{m + \tfrac12M} = \dfrac{{m}(9.8)}{{m} + {M}/2} =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = \tfrac12({M})({a:sig3}) =$ **{T:sig3} N**; $\alpha = a/R =$ **{alpha:sig3} rad/s²**.

drills.title: Rolling down a ramp
drills.prompt: A {shape} rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp, dropping a height of {h} m. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its speed at the bottom in m/s, to 3 significant figures. (For comparison, a frictionless sliding block would reach {vs:num2} m/s.)
drills.solution:
With $I = cMR^2$ and $\omega = v/R$: $Mgh = \tfrac12Mv^2 + \tfrac12cMv^2 = \tfrac12(1 + c)Mv^2$, and for a {shape} $c = {shape:num4}$.

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1 + c}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2(9.8)({h})}{1 + {shape:num4}}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Conservation of angular momentum
drills.prompt: A skater spins at {f} rev/s with moment of inertia {I1} kg·m². She pulls in her arms, reducing her moment of inertia to {pct}% of its original value. Find her new spin rate (rev/s) and her new rotational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
No external torque: $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$, so $f_2 = f_1\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{{f}}{{pct}/100} =$ **{f2:sig3} rev/s**.

New $I_2 = {I2:dp3}$ kg·m² and $\omega_2 = 2\pi f_2$; $K_2 = \tfrac12I_2\omega_2^2 =$ **{K2:sig3} J** (up from {K1:num1} J; her muscles did the work).

drills.title: Balancing a seesaw
drills.prompt: A uniform seesaw is pivoted at its center. A {m1} kg person sits {d1} m from the pivot. How far from the pivot, on the other side, must a {m2} kg person sit to balance it? Give meters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torques about the pivot must cancel (the seesaw's weight and the pivot force act at the pivot): ${m1}g({d1}) = {m2}g\,x$.

$x = \dfrac{{m1}({d1})}{{m2}} =$ **{d2:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Beam on two supports
drills.prompt: A uniform {L} m beam of mass {mb} kg rests on supports at its ends A and B. A {m} kg crate sits {x:num2} m from end A. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the upward force from each support, in newtons to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torques about A: $F_B({L}) = {mb}(9.8)({L}/2) + {m}(9.8)({x:num2})$, so $F_B =$ **{FB:sig3} N**.

Vertical forces: $F_A = ({mb} + {m})(9.8) - F_B =$ **{FA:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Gravitational force and surface gravity
drills.prompt: A planet has mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg and radius ${Rm}\times10^{6}$ m. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², find the acceleration due to gravity at its surface (m/s²) and the weight there of a {m} kg probe (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2} = \dfrac{(6.67\times10^{-11})({Mm}\times10^{{Me}})}{({Rm}\times10^{6})^2} =$ **{gs:sig3} m/s²**.

Weight $= mg = {m}({gs:sig3}) =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Circular orbit speed and period
drills.prompt: A satellite is in a circular orbit {h} km above Earth's surface. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², $M_E = 5.97\times10^{24}$ kg and $R_E = 6.37\times10^{6}$ m, find its orbital speed (m/s) and period (minutes), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Orbit radius from Earth's center: $r = R_E + h = {r:texsci}$ m.

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM_E}{\,r}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{\,v} =$ **{T:sig3} min**.

drills.title: Escape speed
drills.prompt: Find the escape speed (km/s) from the surface of a planet with mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg and radius ${Rm}\times10^{6}$ m, and the speed of a circular orbit just above its surface. Use $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg² and give both speeds in km/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Total energy zero: $\tfrac12mv^2 = \dfrac{GMm}{\,R}$, so $v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{\,R}} =$ **{ve:sig3} km/s**.

Low orbit: $v = \sqrt{GM/R} = v_{\text{esc}}/\sqrt2 =$ **{vo:sig3} km/s**.

drills.title: Stress, strain and stretch of a wire
drills.prompt: A wire of {mat}, {L} m long and {d} mm in diameter, hangs vertically and supports a {load} kg mass. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the stress in the wire (Pa), the strain, and how much the wire stretches (mm), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Force $F = mg = {load}(9.8) = {F:sig4}$ N; area $A = \pi d^2/4 = \pi({d}\times10^{-3})^2/4 = {A:texsci}$ m².

Stress $= F/A = \mathbf{{sig:texsci}}$ Pa. Strain $= \text{stress}/Y = \mathbf{{eps:texsci}}$.

Stretch $\Delta L = \text{strain} \times L = ({eps:texsci})({L}\text{ m}) =$ **{dL:sig3} mm**.

drills.title: Period and frequency of a mass on a spring
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block on a frictionless surface is attached to a spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m. Find the period (s) and the frequency (Hz) of its oscillation, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega = \sqrt{k/m} = \sqrt{{k:dp0}/{m}} = {w:num2}$ rad/s.

$T = 2\pi/\omega = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k} =$ **{T:sig3} s**, and $f = 1/T =$ **{f:sig3} Hz**.

drills.title: Simple pendulum
drills.prompt: A simple pendulum {L} m long swings with small amplitude on {planet}. Find its period in seconds, to 3 significant figures. (Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² on Earth, 1.62 m/s² on the Moon, 3.71 m/s² on Mars.)
drills.solution: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g} = 2\pi\sqrt{{L}/{planet:num2}} =$ **{T:sig3} s**. The bob's mass doesn't matter.

drills.title: Maximum speed and acceleration in SHM
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring ($k = {k:dp0}$ N/m) oscillates with amplitude {Acm} cm. Find its maximum speed, its maximum acceleration, and its speed when it is {x:num4} m from equilibrium. Use m/s and m/s², to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega = \sqrt{k/m} = {w:num4}$ rad/s.

$v_{\max} = A\omega = ({A})({w:num4}) =$ **{vmax:sig3} m/s**; $a_{\max} = A\omega^2 =$ **{amax:sig3} m/s²**.

From energy, $v = \omega\sqrt{A^2 - x^2} = {w:num4}\sqrt{{A}^2 - {x:num4}^2} =$ **{vx:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Wave speed, frequency and wavelength
drills.prompt: A {f} Hz tone travels as {kind} (speed {kind:int} m/s). Find its wavelength (m) and its period (s), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\lambda = v/f = {kind:dp0}/{f:dp0} =$ **{lam:sig3} m**.

$T = 1/f = 1/{f:dp0} = \mathbf{{T:texsci}}$ s.

drills.title: Harmonics of a stretched string
drills.prompt: A string {L} m long with mass {mg} g is fixed at both ends under {F} N of tension. Find the wave speed, the fundamental frequency and the frequency of harmonic $n = {n}$, to 3 significant figures (m/s and Hz).

drills.title: Intensity and decibels
drills.prompt: A small speaker radiates {P} W of sound equally in all directions. At {r} m away, find the intensity (W/m², to 3 significant figures) and the sound intensity level (dB, to 1 decimal place). Use $I_0 = 10^{-12}$ W/m².
drills.solution:
$I = \dfrac{\,P}{4\pi r^2} = \dfrac{{P}}{4\pi({r})^2} = \mathbf{{I:texsci}}$ W/m².

$\beta = 10\log_{10}\dfrac{\,I}{I_0} =$ **{B:num1} dB**.

drills.title: Doppler shift from a moving source
drills.prompt: A siren emits {f} Hz and moves at {vs} m/s past a stationary listener. Using $v = 343$ m/s, find the frequency heard as it approaches and as it recedes, in Hz to 4 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Approaching source: $f' = f\dfrac{v}{v - v_s} = {f:dp0}\cdot\dfrac{343}{343 - {vs}} =$ **{fa:sig4} Hz**.

Receding: $f' = {f:dp0}\cdot\dfrac{343}{343 + {vs}} =$ **{fr:sig4} Hz**.

drills.title: Resonances of an air column
drills.prompt: A pipe {L} m long is {pipe}. Using $v = 343$ m/s, find its fundamental frequency and the next higher resonant frequency, in Hz to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Open at both ends: $f_n = nv/(2L)$, all $n$. Closed at one end: $f_n = nv/(4L)$, odd $n$ only. This pipe is {pipe}.

$f_1 =$ **{f1:sig3} Hz**, and the next resonance is **{f2:sig3} Hz** ($2f_1$ for an open pipe, $3f_1$ for a closed one).

drills.title: Beats
drills.prompt: Two tuning forks of {f1} Hz and {f2} Hz are struck together. Find the beat frequency and the frequency of the tone you hear throbbing, in Hz (the tone to 1 decimal place).
drills.solution:
$f_{\text{beat}} = |f_1 - f_2| = |{f1} - {f2}| =$ **{fb} Hz**.

The tone heard is the average frequency, $\tfrac12({f1} + {f2}) =$ **{favg:num1} Hz**, getting louder and softer {fb} times per second.

drills.title: Decay of a damped oscillator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring ($k = {k:dp0}$ N/m) is damped by a force $-bv$ with $b = {b}$ kg/s. It starts oscillating with amplitude {A0} cm. Find its quality factor $Q$, the time for the amplitude to fall to half (s), and the amplitude after {tt} s (cm), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$Q = \dfrac{\sqrt{mk}}{\,b} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{m}({k:dp0})}}{{b}} =$ **{Q:sig3}**, so the damping is light and the mass oscillates.

The amplitude decays as $e^{-\gamma t}$ with $\gamma = b/2m = {b}/(2 \times {m}) = {gam:sig4}$ s⁻¹. It halves when $e^{-\gamma t} = \tfrac12$: $t = \ln 2/\gamma =$ **{th:sig3} s**.

After {tt} s: $A = {A0}\,e^{-({gam:sig4})({tt})} =$ **{At:sig3} cm**.

drills.title: Critical damping and the damped frequency
drills.prompt: A mass of {m} kg hangs on a spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m. Find the damping constant that would make it critically damped (kg/s). If the actual damping constant is $b = {b}$ kg/s, find the angular frequency at which it oscillates (rad/s). Give both to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Critical damping means $\gamma = \omega_0$, i.e. $b_c = 2\sqrt{mk} = 2\sqrt{{m}({k:dp0})} =$ **{bc:sig3} kg/s**.

The actual $b = {b}$ kg/s is smaller, so the motion is underdamped. $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = {w0:sig4}$ rad/s and $\gamma = b/2m = {gam:sig4}$ s⁻¹, so $\omega' = \sqrt{\omega_0^2 - \gamma^2} =$ **{wd:sig3} rad/s**, noticeably below $\omega_0$.

drills.title: Steady-state amplitude of a driven oscillator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring ($k = {k:dp0}$ N/m, damping constant $b = {b}$ kg/s) is driven by a force $F_0\cos\omega t$ with $F_0 = {F0}$ N. Find the steady-state amplitude when $\omega = {w}$ rad/s, and when it is driven at its natural frequency. Give both in cm to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m} = {w0:sig4}$ rad/s and $2\gamma = b/m = {g2:sig4}$ s⁻¹.

$A = \dfrac{F_0/m}{\sqrt{(\omega_0^2 - \omega^2)^2 + (2\gamma\omega)^2}}$ with $\omega = {w}$ rad/s gives **{A:sig3} cm**.

At $\omega_0$ only damping limits it: $A = \dfrac{F_0}{b\,\omega_0} = \dfrac{{F0}}{{b}({w0:sig4})} =$ **{Ar:sig3} cm** (that is $Q = {Q:sig3}$ times the static stretch $F_0/k$).

drills.title: Power carried by a wave on a string
drills.prompt: A string with linear mass density {mug} g/m is under {F} N of tension. A sinusoidal wave of frequency {f} Hz and amplitude {Amm} mm travels along it. Find the wave speed (m/s) and the average power the wave carries (W), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\mu = {mu:dp3}$ kg/m, so $v = \sqrt{F_T/\mu} = \sqrt{{F}/{mu:dp3}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$\omega = 2\pi({f}) = {w:sig4}$ rad/s and $A = {A:dp4}$ m, so $P_{\text{avg}} = \tfrac12\mu A^2\omega^2v = \tfrac12({mu:dp3})({A:dp4})^2({w:sig4})^2({v:sig4}) =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Pressure at depth
drills.prompt: Find the gauge pressure and the absolute pressure {h} m below the surface of {fluid}. Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² and $P_{\text{atm}} = 1.013\times10^5$ Pa, and give both in pascals to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Gauge: $\rho gh = ({fluid:dp0})(9.8)({h}) = \mathbf{{Pg:texsci}}$ Pa.

Absolute: $P_{\text{atm}} + \rho gh = \mathbf{{Pabs:texsci}}$ Pa, about {natm:num2} atm.

drills.title: Apparent weight and floating fraction
drills.prompt: An object of density {rho:dp0} kg/m³ and volume {Vc:dp0} cm³ is held completely under water (density 1000 kg/m³). Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the buoyant force and its apparent weight (weight minus buoyant force; a negative value means it would float up if released), both in newtons to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$V = {Vc:dp0}\text{ cm}^3 = {V:texsci}$ m³. $F_B = \rho_{\text{water}}Vg = 1000({V:texsci})(9.8) =$ **{FB:sig3} N**.

Weight $= \rho Vg = {W:num2}$ N, so weight minus buoyancy $=$ **{app:sig3} N**. A positive value is the force you must hold it up with; a negative value means it is less dense than water and you must push it down.

drills.title: Hydraulic lift
drills.prompt: A hydraulic lift has pistons of diameter {d1} cm and {d2} cm. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², what force on the small piston supports a {m} kg car on the large one, and how far must the small piston move in total to raise the car {h} m? Give the force in newtons and the distance in meters, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Area ratio $= (d_2/d_1)^2 = ({d2}/{d1})^2 = {ratio:sig4}$.

Pascal: $F_1 = \dfrac{mg}{A_2/A_1} = \dfrac{{m:dp0}(9.8)}{{ratio:sig4}} =$ **{F1:sig3} N**.

Equal volumes: $d_1 = {h}({ratio:sig4}) =$ **{s1:sig3} m** (many pump strokes).

drills.title: Continuity equation
drills.prompt: Water flows at {v1} m/s through a pipe of diameter {D1} cm that narrows to {D2} cm. Find the speed in the narrow section (m/s) and the flow rate in liters per second, to 3 significant figures.

drills.title: Pressure in a narrowing horizontal pipe
drills.prompt: Water flows through a horizontal pipe. Where the pressure is {P1k} kPa the speed is {v1} m/s. At a narrower section the speed is {v2} m/s. What is the pressure there, in kPa to 3 significant figures? (Water density 1000 kg/m³.)
drills.solution:
Same height, so $P_1 + \tfrac12\rho v_1^2 = P_2 + \tfrac12\rho v_2^2$:

$P_2 = {P1k}\times10^3 + \tfrac12(1000)({v1}^2 - {v2}^2) = {P2:int}$ Pa $=$ **{P2k:sig3} kPa**. Faster flow, lower pressure.

drills.title: Draining tank (Torricelli)
drills.prompt: A large open tank has a hole of area {a} cm² located {h} m below the water surface. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the speed of the emerging water (m/s) and the initial flow rate in L/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torricelli: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({h})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$Q = Av = ({a}\times10^{-4})({v:num2})$ m³/s $=$ **{Q:sig3} L/s**.

drills.title: Final temperature of a mixture
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg block of {metal} ($c = {metal:dp0}$ J/(kg·K)) at {T1}°C is dropped into {m2} kg of water ($c = 4186$ J/(kg·K)) at {T2}°C in an insulated cup. Ignoring the cup, find the final temperature in °C, to the nearest 0.1°C.

drills.title: Heat to melt and warm ice
drills.prompt: How much heat is needed to turn {m} kg of ice at {Ti}°C into water at {Tf}°C? Use $c_{\text{ice}} = 2100$ J/(kg·K), $L_f = 3.34\times10^5$ J/kg and $c_{\text{water}} = 4186$ J/(kg·K), and give the answer in joules to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Warm the ice to 0°C: ${m}(2100)(0 - ({Ti})) = {Q1:dp0}$ J.

Melt it: ${m}(3.34\times10^5) = {Q2:dp0}$ J.

Warm the water: ${m}(4186)({Tf}) = {Q3:dp0}$ J.

Total: $Q = \mathbf{{Q:texsci}}$ J.

drills.title: Thermal expansion
drills.prompt: A {L} m long piece of {mat} warms from {T1}°C to {T2}°C. By how many millimeters does it lengthen? Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\Delta L = \alpha L\Delta T = ({mat}\times10^{-6})({L})({T2} - ({T1})) =$ **{dL:sig3} mm**. (A Celsius difference equals a kelvin difference.)

drills.title: Heat conduction through a wall
drills.prompt: A {A} m² panel of {k} is {Lcm} cm thick. The temperature difference across it is {dT} K. Find the rate of heat conduction (W) and the heat lost in one hour (kJ), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\dfrac{Q}{t} = \dfrac{kA\Delta T}{L} = \dfrac{({k:num2})({A})({dT})}{{Lcm}/100} =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

In 3600 s: **{E:sig3} kJ**.

drills.title: Ideal gas law
drills.prompt: {n} mol of an ideal gas at {TC}°C occupies {VL} L. What is its pressure, in pascals to 3 significant figures? ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
Convert: $T = {TC} + 273.15 = {T:num2}$ K, $V = {VL}\times10^{-3}$ m³.

$P = \dfrac{nRT}{V} = \dfrac{({n})(8.314)({T:num2})}{{VL}\times10^{-3}} = \mathbf{{P:texsci}}$ Pa.

drills.title: Combined gas law
drills.prompt: A gas occupies {V1} L at {P1} atm and {T1} K. What volume does it occupy at {P2} atm and {T2} K? Give liters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$, so $V_2 = V_1\cdot\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\cdot\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = {V1}\cdot\dfrac{{P1}}{{P2}}\cdot\dfrac{{T2}}{{T1}} =$ **{V2:sig3} L**.

drills.title: RMS speed and average kinetic energy
drills.prompt: Find the rms speed of {gas} molecules at {T} K (m/s) and their average translational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K), $k_B = 1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K)
drills.solution:
$v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3(8.314)({T:dp0})}{{gas:sig3}}} =$ **{v:int} m/s** ($M$ in kg/mol).

$\overline K = \tfrac32k_BT = \mathbf{{K:texsci}}$ J (the same for every gas at this temperature).

drills.title: First law of thermodynamics
drills.prompt: During a process a gas absorbs {Q} J of heat (negative means it releases heat) and does {W} J of work on its surroundings (negative means work is done on it). Find the change in its internal energy, in joules.
drills.solution: $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = Q - W = ({Q}) - ({W}) =$ **{dU} J**, with $Q$ into the gas and $W$ done by the gas.

drills.title: Constant-pressure process for a monatomic gas
drills.prompt: {n} mol of a monatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure, raising its temperature by {dT} K. Find the work done by the gas, the change in internal energy, and the heat added, in joules to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
$W = P\Delta V = nR\Delta T = ({n})(8.314)({dT}) =$ **{W:sig3} J**.

$\Delta E_{\text{int}} = \tfrac32nR\Delta T =$ **{dU:sig3} J**.

$Q = \Delta E_{\text{int}} + W = \tfrac52nR\Delta T =$ **{Q:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Isothermal expansion
drills.prompt: {n} mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally at {T} K until its volume is {r} times larger. How much work does it do, and how much heat does it absorb? Give joules to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
$W = \displaystyle\int P\,dV = nRT\ln\frac{V_f}{V_i} = ({n})(8.314)({T})\ln {r} =$ **{W:sig3} J**.

Isothermal: $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = 0$, so $Q = W =$ **{W:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Carnot efficiency and heat rejected
drills.prompt: An ideal (Carnot) engine runs between a hot reservoir at {TH}°C and a cold one at {TC}°C. Find its efficiency (as a decimal) and, if it absorbs {QH} J per cycle, the work output and the heat rejected per cycle, in joules. Give all three to 3 significant figures, and convert with $T = T_C + 273$.
drills.solution:
In kelvins, $T_H = {TH} + 273$ and $T_C = {TC} + 273$. $e = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H} =$ **{e:sig3}**.

$W = eQ_H =$ **{W:sig3} J**; $Q_C = Q_H - W =$ **{QC:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Engine efficiency from work and exhaust heat
drills.prompt: An engine does {W} J of work per cycle and exhausts {QC} J of heat. How much heat does it absorb per cycle (J), and what is its efficiency (as a decimal to 3 significant figures)?
drills.solution:
First law over a cycle: $Q_H = W + Q_C = {W:dp0} + {QC:dp0} =$ **{QH:dp0} J**.

$e = W/Q_H =$ **{e:sig3}**.

drills.title: Entropy change of melting and of heating
drills.prompt: {m} kg of ice at 0°C melts, and the water is then warmed to {T2}°C. Find the entropy change for (a) the melting and (b) the warming, in J/K to 3 significant figures. ($L_f = 3.34\times10^5$ J/kg, $c = 4186$ J/(kg·K), 0°C = 273.15 K)
drills.solution:
(a) Constant temperature: $\Delta S = \dfrac{mL_f}{T} = \dfrac{{m}(3.34\times10^5)}{273.15} =$ **{S1:sig3} J/K**.

(b) $\Delta S = \displaystyle\int\frac{mc\,dT}{T} = mc\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} = {m}(4186)\ln\frac{{T2} + 273.15}{273.15} =$ **{S2:sig3} J/K**.
